diagnoses.mechanism: The prompt's evidence was complete. It held every key paragraph verbatim: SOURCE 2 (b) cosmetics generally incl. eye area, GMP; SOURCE 4 (c)(1) § 70.25; SOURCE 5 (c)(2) 'Cosmetics containing carmine that are not subject to the requirements of § 701.3 ... shall specifically declare'; SOURCE 6 (d) exempt. The paragraph-by-paragraph list in the draft is correct. The lead answer misapplied two things. (1) It turned the (c)(2) restrictive relative clause into a premise about the user's product: 'because the product contains carmine and is not subject to the requirements of § 701.3, it must ... declare'. A retail blush normally IS subject to 701.3, so the true answer depends on that condition. (2) It invented a causal link between eye-area use and labeling: 'because the blush ... is intended for use in or near the area of the eye, labeling requirements apply' and 'This requirement applies regardless ... since the term area of the eye includes ... [7]'. The second error came from the 70.3(s) companion. That companion was appended to the question text as '(21 CFR 73.2087, 70.3(s))', made requested provision r2, and listed FIRST in the exhaustive item list, so the model felt obliged to apply the definition in the lead. The validator caught only the eye-area sentence, and only as a low_overlap warning. It caught nothing on the 701.3 premise, because the condition wording was copied verbatim and only the logical role changed. The secondary stage is the closest enum value: the problem is how the companion was presented, not a wrong pick.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong: asserts the blush is 'not subject to § 701.3' (a condition made into fact), and says labeling applies because of eye-area use. Missing: the correct conditional (if the cosmetic is subject to 701.3, carmine is declared through ingredient labeling; if not, it needs the specific 'Contains carmine' declaration).
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add a deterministic 'condition asserted as premise' check. For each source condition phrase (a restrictive relative clause such as 'that are not subject to', 'if', 'unless', 'when', 'except'), flag any answer sentence that restates the phrase as a fact about the user's product after a premise marker ('because', 'since', 'as it is', 'the product is/does'). Route the sentence to repair, which rewrites it as 'if <condition>, <requirement>'. Separately, present companion definitions as supporting context, not as requested provisions: do not append them to the QUESTION line, and list them after the keyed section's items rather than first. The check only fires on a condition phrase copied into a premise frame, so correctly conditional answers are unaffected. The companion change alters prompt order for every question with a companion, so A/B it on the 100Q set.

diagnoses.mechanism: The keyed paragraph (d)(1) is in the prompt as SOURCE 8 ('The label of the color additive bismuth citrate shall bear ... labeling in accordance with the provisions of § 70.25'). It is also named in the 'its sub-requirements' line as '[8]'. The model covered (c)(1) [5], (c)(2) [6], the (d)(2) warning [10] and (e) [11], but skipped [8]. Two prompt features invited the skip. (1) The answer shape was 'focused on the requested provision', with focus terms taken from the question ('limits, warnings, certification, status'). The other listing questions got 'every item, listed separately (exhaustive)', and (d)(1) is neither a limit nor a warning. (2) The sub-requirements line is garbled by a sentence splitter that cuts at periods inside numbers and section references ('shall not be in excess of 2 [5]', 'provisions of § 70 [8]'). It also prints empty items (' [3]', ' [6]', ' [10]'), so [8] reads as a fragment and not as a requirement. The key is arguably broad here: the user asked about use limits, warnings and certification, and (d)(1) covers labeling of the color additive itself (supplier-side), not a cosmetic warning.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: (d)(1), § 70.25 labeling of the color additive. Everything else is correct.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Fix the sub-requirements extractor so it never splits at a digit.digit decimal or a '§ N.N' reference, and drop empty entries; this applies to every prompt that prints the line. (2) Choose the answer shape by the keyed section's paragraph structure as well as the question words: when the question asks for 'requirements/warnings/labeling/certification' of a listed substance, use the exhaustive item list. (3) Optionally, add a post-draft coverage step for exhaustive or listing shapes: any sub-requirement source the prompt names but the answer never cites is appended as a verbatim, cited sentence. That only adds verbatim text, so it cannot introduce unsupported claims. Expect slightly longer answers; check against the frozen set for redundancy flags.

diagnoses.mechanism: The prompt had the whole section ((a)-(e)), and the first draft was substantively right. Shampoos are permitted under (c) at GMP amounts; body wash is not authorized ('not permitted for use in body washes, as no such use is authorized'); labeling follows § 70.25 [5]; certification is exempt [6]. The validator raised two unsupported_claim errors. The first was the absence sentence the prompt's own ANSWER FORMAT asks for ('say that these provisions impose none'), here 'These provisions impose no specific limits on the amount ...' at 20% overlap. The second was a negative inference, 'The use in body washes is not addressed in any provision, so it is not permitted' at 0% overlap. An absence or exclusion claim has, by construction, few content words in the source, so lexical-overlap support always fails for it. Both flagged sentences repeat the supported first sentence, which already denies body wash. Yet the whole answer was withheld rather than having those two sentences dropped.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Delivered nothing. A correct draft was withheld because of two redundant absence or exclusion sentences.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (a) Classify scoped absence sentences ('this/these provision(s) impose/set/specify/state no X') as absence claims. Verify them against the cited Uses/restrictions paragraph, accepting them when that paragraph has no numeric or limiting term for the dimension named, instead of using content-word overlap. Keep unscoped forms ('no regulation anywhere', 'FDA lacks authority', 'under current regulations') as errors, to preserve the false-denial protection. (b) In the withhold decision, if an unsupported sentence's proposition is already stated by a supported sentence (high overlap with an earlier sentence that passed), drop that sentence and deliver the rest instead of withholding. Both rules only remove or reclassify sentences, never add text. Fabricated positive claims keep the existing check. Replay the 100Q drafts offline to confirm no FAIL becomes a wrong delivered answer.

diagnoses.mechanism: Every keyed paragraph is in the prompt: (a)(1) SOURCE 2, (b) SOURCE 6, (c) SOURCE 7, (d) SOURCE 8. The model treated the (a)(2)(ii) diluent rule as a condition on the finished nail polish: 'may be used ... provided that the product is intended for external use and complies with the specified diluent restrictions'. The packing invites that. The parent lead-in, which names the subject ('(2) Color additive mixtures of guanine may contain the following diluents:'), is SOURCE 3. The children are separate sources with no subject: SOURCE 5 is '(ii) For coloring externally applied cosmetics, only those diluents listed in § 73.1001(b) and, in addition, nitrocellulose.' Read alone, SOURCE 5 looks like a restriction on externally applied cosmetics, and the model cites [5] for its product-level condition. The evidence was present but stripped of its subject (hence the secondary stage). The validator also raised a false unsupported_figure error, '73.1001'. That number appears verbatim in SOURCES 4 and 5 ('§ 73.1001(a)(1)', '§ 73.1001(b)'); the draft wrote '§73.1001'. The error triggered a correction pass, which kept the misreading in the delivered lead.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong: the lead makes permission conditional on the product being externally applied and containing only § 73.1001(b) diluents. Guanine is permitted in cosmetics generally, including the eye area, at GMP amounts, and the diluent rule limits color-additive mixtures, not the cosmetic.
diagnoses.fix_detail: When a source is a child subparagraph whose parent ends with ':' (an enumerated lead-in), pack it with a one-line 'Context:' carrying the parent's lead-in clause (e.g., 'Context: Color additive mixtures of guanine may contain the following diluents'). This is lighter than the grouped-subparagraph packing rejected on 20 Oct, which merged whole groups and cost budget. Also fix the figure check (see the 82.1328 row) so false figure errors stop sending correct drafts to repair. The Context line adds a few dozen characters only for colon-led children, so the budget effect is small. A/B it on 4B before keeping it, because the earlier grouping regressed on 1.7B.

diagnoses.mechanism: The question names 'FD&C Blue No. 1' and 'FD&C Blue No. 1 Aluminum Lake', but the picker replied '21 CFR 74.2340' (heading 'FD&C Red No. 40.'). The prompt therefore holds only 74.2340 plus the 70.3(s) companion; the key's 74.2101 is absent (measured in-prompt = False). 74.2340 looked plausible because its (b) text matches the question's shape, 'only FD&C Red No. 40 and FD&C Red No. 40 Aluminum Lake may be safely used in coloring cosmetics intended for use in the area of the eye', with aluminum lake, eye area and an eye-shadow-like use. The LLM picker matched those structural features and ignored the color name and number. The model noticed the mismatch, but concluded 'neither ... is permitted', a false denial; the validator correctly withheld it. The packet does not list the candidates. If 74.2101 was not among them, the stage is RETRIEVAL_MISSING instead.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong section (74.2340, Red No. 40, instead of 74.2101, Blue No. 1). Missing: the (c)(1)/(c)(2) permissions and the (e) Part 80 certification.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add a named-substance consistency guard after the picker. Extract color-additive names from the question (pattern '(Ext\. )?(FD&C|D&C) <Color> No\. <N>( Aluminum Lake)?', plus listed names such as 'carmine' or 'guanine'). If the picked section's heading names a different color additive, reject the pick. Choose the candidate whose heading matches the name exactly, or run a direct heading lookup in Parts 73/74/82, where headings are the substance names. Prefer the Part 74 subpart C cosmetic listing for a cosmetic question. The guard fires only on an explicit name mismatch, so picks that already match are untouched.

diagnoses.mechanism: The model was not called; the deterministic listing composer answered from the right evidence (74.2260(a)-(d), 70.3(v), plus 82.1260 and 82.1050). The question has three parts: can we use it, is there a use limit, does it need certification. The composer wrote direct answer lines for only the first two ('Body lotion: permitted.' and 'Use limit: no percentage is stated ...'). Certification got no 'Certification: required' line. It is answered only by quoting 74.2260(d) verbatim: 'All batches of D&C Orange No. 11 shall be certified'. That paragraph names a different color than the section heading (D&C Orange No. 10), a misprint in the source, and the composer passed it through unflagged. The answer therefore never says that Orange No. 10 needs certification. The composer also added a near-duplicate of 82.1260 ('repeated_statement' warning).
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: an explicit statement that D&C Orange No. 10 batches must be certified under Part 80, and a note that (d) as printed says 'Orange No. 11'.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Have the composer emit one direct answer line for each question facet it detects (use, limit, certification, labeling), mapping certification to the paragraph with the 'Certification' or 'Exemption from certification' heading or lead word: 'Certification: required — all batches must be certified under part 80 [4]', or 'exempt [n]'. (2) Add an entity-consistency note: when a quoted paragraph names a listed substance different from its section heading (same naming pattern, different number or color), append '(as printed; this section concerns <heading substance>)'. (3) Suppress a quotation that nearly duplicates one already composed. These changes are deterministic and only affect composed_from_listing answers.

diagnoses.mechanism: Both keyed provisions are in the prompt verbatim: SOURCE 1 82.1328 ('... to the requirements of § 74.1328 (a)(1) and (b)') and SOURCE 2 82.1050. The draft answered everything the key asks: the conformance requirement, 'This provision does not restrict use of D&C Red No. 28 for bath bombs', and 82.1050 certification for use only in drugs and cosmetics. The 82.1050 sentence was slightly loosely worded. The only error-severity finding was unsupported_figure '74', and it is false. The section number 74.1328 is in the source, which writes '§ 74.1328 (a)(1)' with a space while the draft wrote '§ 74.1328(a)(1)'. The figure check compares number tokens with citation formatting attached (§ spacing, attached paragraph designators), so a cross-reference section number in the draft does not match the same reference in the source. The same false error appears on 82.1330 ('74'), 82.1602 ('74.1602', where the source has '§ 74.1602(a)(1)' and the draft '§74.1602') and 73.2329 ('73.1001').
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Delivered nothing. A correct draft was withheld on a false figure error.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Canonicalize citations before the figure check, on both the source and the draft side: drop '§'/'§§', collapse whitespace, and split off paragraph designators so '§ 74.1328 (a)(1)', '§74.1328(a)(1)' and '74.1328' all reduce to section '74.1328' plus paragraph '(a)(1)'. Treat numbers inside a section citation as citations, accepted when the section appears in any supplied source's text or citation, not as quantities. Keep the numeric check strict for real quantities (percent, ppm, days). This only removes false errors on cross-references; fabricated percentages and amounts are still caught. Replay the 100Q drafts to count unblocked answers and confirm none is wrong.

diagnoses.mechanism: 82.1330 and 82.1050 are both in the prompt verbatim. The draft gave the conformance requirement to § 74.1330(a)(1) and (b), the absence answer the question asks for ('This provision sets no specific limits on quantity, usage, or application ...'), and the 82.1050 point. Two error findings blocked it. (1) A false unsupported_figure '74': the source writes '§ 74.1330 (a)(1)' and the draft '§ 74.1330(a)(1)', the same citation-normalization defect as 82.1328. (2) unsupported_claim at 30% overlap on the absence sentence, which is exactly the 'say that these provisions impose none' statement the ANSWER FORMAT asks for. The fallback then delivered the verbatim provisions with no applied answer, so 'does it set limits' went unanswered and the row scored PF. A minor overreach in the draft ('use ... in an eyeshadow palette is permitted if the batch conforms to § 82.5') would have needed trimming, but the key elements were present.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing from the delivered answer: the statement that 82.1330 sets no use restriction or quantitative limit, which the draft had.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Apply the same two validator changes. (1) Canonicalize citations before the figure check (see the 82.1328 row). (2) Verify scoped absence claims ('this provision sets/imposes no ...') by checking that the cited sources contain no limiting terms ('not more than', 'percent', 'not to exceed', 'only', 'may not', 'restricted to') for that dimension, instead of using lexical overlap. Accept them when that check passes, and keep unscoped denials as errors. The prompt's own instruction and the validator then agree. Frozen-set replay should show withheld-to-delivered changes only on rows whose absence statements are true.

diagnoses.mechanism: 82.1602 and 82.1050 are both in the prompt verbatim. The draft answered both questions: the conformance requirement, plus 'This provision does not restrict its use in toning shampoos' and 'The provisions do not impose any specific limits, restrictions, or usage conditions ...'. The validator raised two errors. (1) A false unsupported_figure '74.1602': the source has '§ 74.1602(a)(1)', and the draft's bare '§74.1602.' did not match because of the attached paragraph designator and § spacing. (2) unsupported_claim (0%) on the absence sentence. The correction pass then delivered a rewritten answer with both absence sentences removed, including 'does not restrict its use in toning shampoos', which was never flagged. The validator did not withhold the answer outright; its false and over-strict findings made the repair strip the one sentence that answered 'does it restrict use?'. That repair behavior is the 'OTHER' secondary, and the stage is the closest enum value for 'repair removed good content'. The delivered answer only restates the provisions, hence PF.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing from the delivered answer: '82.1602 states no use restriction or quantitative limit', which the draft had and the repair removed.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Apply the same two changes: citation canonicalization in the figure check, and dedicated verification of scoped absence claims. In addition, limit the correction pass to removing or rewriting only the sentences named by error findings; a finding with no sentence attached, like this figure error, should not license a whole-answer rewrite. If a facet of the question (here 'does it restrict use') loses its only answering sentence during repair, re-run the absence check or keep the original sentence. This protects correct answers without letting unsupported positive claims through.

diagnoses.mechanism: The right section was picked (82.2051), and SOURCE 1 holds the full (a)(1) text: all ten substrata, branch (i) (a straight color that is already a Na/K/Ba/Ca salt) and branch (ii) (a salt made with Na/K/Al/Ba/Ca/Sr/Zr). SOURCE 3 holds the (a)(2) limits. The model paraphrased (a)(1) into one sentence. It cut the substrata to 'such as clay, titanium dioxide, or zinc oxide', dropped branch (i), and merged the two branches into 'formed by combining the basic radical calcium with one of the listed straight colors'. The answer paragraph adds confusing framing ('not restricted by the substrate alone'). The validator had no findings because every shortened statement is still a subset of the source. Nothing checks that a listed enumeration was kept whole, and the deterministic composer did not handle this listing question.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: the 82.2051(a)(1)(i) branch and the full substrata and basic-radical lists ('such as' truncation). (a)(1)(i) and (ii) are merged into one misleading condition.
diagnoses.fix_detail: For answers with the 'every item, listed separately (exhaustive)' shape, build the paragraph-by-paragraph part with the deterministic composer from each source paragraph's text (verbatim or lightly normalized, keeping (i)/(ii) branches and full comma series). The model then writes only the applied first paragraph. Add a validator check on that paragraph: if a sentence cites a source whose text has an enumerated series of 3 or more items or (i)/(ii) alternatives, and it shortens the series with 'such as'/'e.g.' or keeps only one branch, raise an incompleteness flag. This only changes exhaustive-shape outputs and never adds content beyond the source text, so it cannot add unsupported claims. Measure on the other lake and listing rows (82.1051, 82.2051, 70.19) for a non-regression check.

diagnoses.mechanism: The pick was right (82.705, plus 82.50 as companion), but both supplied provisions are pointers. 82.705 says 'conform ... to § 74.705(a)(1) and (b)' and 82.50 says 'conforms to the requirements of § 82.5'. § 82.5 (lead ≤0.001%, As2O3 ≤0.00014%, heavy metals trace) is not in the prompt, so no answer could state the limits the key requires. Separately, the validator withheld a draft that faithfully restated both provisions. Its only error was unsupported_figure '74'. That number comes from the draft's '§74.705(a)(1)' (no space), while the source writes '§ 74.705 (a)(1)'. The figure extractor treats a citation-shaped token as a bare figure on one side but not the other, which is a false positive. The verbatim fallback was delivered and scored PF. The unblocked draft would also have been PF, because 82.5 is missing.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing evidence: 21 CFR 82.5 numeric limits. The validator also falsely flagged '74', which is part of the section number 74.705 and is present in SOURCE 1.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add a one-hop cross-reference companion. It fires only when a promoted or companion provision's operative text is a pointer clause ('conform(s) to the requirements of § X', 'specified in § X', 'in accordance with § X') and the prompt is far under budget. In that case, add § X (or the named paragraphs) as a companion source. This is narrower than the earlier xref switch, which lost out to budget pressure on general questions. Here prompts carry 2 short sources, so no displacement occurs. It covers every Part 82 color (82.50/82.1050/82.2050 → 82.5) and 73.x monographs that point to 73.1xxx. Also fix the validator: strip citation-shaped tokens (§ N.N with or without a space, with paragraph designators) from figure extraction on both draft and sources before comparing.

diagnoses.mechanism: The question names 'FD&C Yellow No. 6' and 'Part 82'. The picker replied '21 CFR 82.50 General. (Listing of Certified Provision', choosing the generic subpart B section over the color-specific 82.706, whose heading is the exact substance name. The companion added was 70.3(j) (the straight color definition), which is low value. The prompt therefore has neither 82.706 (conform to 74.706(a)(1),(b)) nor 82.5 (numeric limits). The model faithfully restated 82.50 and 70.3(j), and the scorers marked PF for the missing 82.706 and 82.5 elements. The twin question COS-82.705-Q1 picked 82.705 with 82.50 as companion, so the picker is inconsistent on identical templates. 'pick right = True' is a measurement artifact: 82.50 is in the key, but it is the secondary provision.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong pick: 82.50 instead of 82.706. Missing evidence: 82.706 and the 82.5 limits.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Run a deterministic pre-picker before the LLM picker: if the question contains a substance or color name that, after normalization, exactly equals a candidate section heading (e.g. 'FD&C Yellow No. 6.'), select that section. Then add its subpart's 'General' section as a companion, as already happens for 82.705. Combine this with the one-hop pointer companion (82.50 → 82.5). An exact heading-name match is a high-precision signal and only fires when a named entity appears in the question, so questions without a named substance are unaffected. Packet does not show the candidate list; confirm 82.706 was a candidate (likely, given the exact heading match).

diagnoses.mechanism: The pick and the evidence were complete: 70.10(b)(1), (b)(2) and (b)(3) are verbatim in SOURCES 6-8. The draft's cited body correctly states all three key elements. It then appended uncited gloss sentences with no [n] marker, which breaks the format rule. One was 'The regulations impose no requirement for pre-approval or specific labeling ... if applicable', an unscoped negative claim that is misleading because an unlisted colorant needs listing. Another was 'The conditions in §70.10(b)(1) and (b)(2) are the only determinants...'. The validator correctly flagged these as invented_condition and unsupported_claim errors. Withholding is all-or-nothing, so a correct and complete answer was discarded and the user saw 'could not be validated'. The answer format's clauses 'say that these provisions impose none' and 'say which part they leave open' invite exactly this kind of sentence.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Two or three uncited, unsupported commentary sentences ('regulations impose no requirement for pre-approval or labeling', 'only determinants') sank an otherwise correct (b)(1)-(3) answer.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add a sentence-excision repair. A sentence is removed only if all of these hold: (a) it carries no source marker, (b) it fails support (unsupported_claim or invented_condition), and (c) it is not the first, direct-answer sentence. After removal, re-run the full validator on the remainder. Deliver only if no error-level findings remain and paragraph-level completeness still covers every requested item or sub-requirement the draft addressed. Never remove a clause inside a sentence: that is the known false-PASS route via invented_conditions_removed. Removing whole uncited sentences cannot make a conditional requirement unconditional. As a companion change, narrow the 'impose none' instruction to a fixed scoped template ('These provisions impose no X') so the model stops producing unscoped 'the regulations impose no...' sentences.

diagnoses.mechanism: All of 70.19(a)-(r) was in the prompt, and the itemized list in the draft is correct. The answer-first paragraph, however, misreads the text. It says 'if withdrawn within 30 days, a refund of $1,600.00 is due under 70.19(f)', but the source says the deposit is returned LESS $1,600 (net $1,000). It says the $600 rule applies 'regardless of whether the withdrawal occurs within 30 days', which contradicts (f). It attributes the 6-month resubmission deposit to (f) instead of (g). The validator withheld the draft, but only for a spurious reason: unsupported_figure '75', from the draft's '$75 per member per day' against the source's '$75.00'. That is a currency-normalization false positive. The real errors passed undetected, because $1,600.00 does appear in the source. So the block was right, but for the wrong reason.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong: the 30-day withdrawal is stated as a $1,600 refund (it is a $1,600 deduction), 'regardless of 30 days' contradicts (f), and resubmission is miscited as (f) instead of (g). The validator only flagged a false '75' figure mismatch.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Canonicalize figures before comparing ($75 = $75.00 = 75; strip thousands separators and trailing .00) so the false positive disappears. (2) Extend provision_citation_mismatch to inline-named provisions such as 'under 21 CFR 70.19(f)'. If the sentence's distinctive content (e.g. 'resubmitted within 6 months') matches a different sibling paragraph's source far better than the named one, raise an error. This catches the (f)/(g) miscitation, and the per-statement citation rule is already an open decision. (3) Add an amount-role check: a figure the source presents as a deduction ('less $X', 'reduced by') must not appear in the draft as the refunded or returned amount ('refund of $X'). Fix (1) alone would release a wrong answer, so ship it only together with (2) and (3). Re-measure on all rows with dollar amounts.

diagnoses.mechanism: The question explicitly asks how 'FDA's definitions classify the lake, the blend and the oil'. The picker latched onto 'D&C Red lake' and chose 82.1051 (Lakes (D&C)), a certification and specification section. The definition companions added only 70.3(l) (lake), because companion matching is by defined term and 'blend' and 'carrier/oil' do not lexically match 'mixture' (70.3(k)) or 'diluent' (70.3(m)). Even 70.3(j) (straight color), a term used inside the included (l) definition, was not added. With (j), (k) and (m) missing, the model wrongly said the blend 'is not explicitly defined' and never called the oil a diluent. It also miscited 82.1050 inside an 82.1051(a)(2) sentence. The validator correctly withheld the draft (provision_citation_mismatch, unsupported_claim). MEASURED 'key section in prompt = True' only reflects section-level 70.3; just paragraph (l) was present.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong primary section (82.1051). Missing: 70.3(j), 70.3(k) (mixture) and 70.3(m) (diluent).
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Route on question intent: when the question asks what something 'is', how it is 'defined' or 'classified', or mentions 'definitions', make the governing Definitions section (70.3 for color additives) the primary pick, with substance or specification sections as companions only. (2) Add definition closure in companions: after a definition is included, also include definitions in the same section for defined terms its text uses ((l) → 'straight color' (j)), and definitions whose body shares the question's role words ('mixture', 'mixed', 'carrier', 'facilitate'). Cap this at the budget. Intent routing fires only on explicit definitional wording, and closure only adds same-section definition paragraphs, so named-provision questions are unaffected.

diagnoses.mechanism: The question asks about a color additive petition with cosmetic and food uses whose data do not show all uses safe at the proposed levels. That is the 70.45 safe-tolerance allocation procedure. The picker replied '21 CFR 740.10, FD&C Act §' and chose the cosmetic warning-label section on unsubstantiated safety, probably on the heading overlap 'cosmetic' plus 'safety'. 70.45's heading ('Allocation of color additives') shares no words with the question, though its body closely mirrors it (petition, data, safe, uses, levels proposed). 70.45 is entirely absent from the prompt. The model then forced 740.10 onto the petition facts ('a warning must be included'), and the validator correctly withheld the draft (condition_not_in_cited_source, unsupported_claim). The packet does not show the candidate list, so it cannot be confirmed whether 70.45 was a candidate (pick error) or never retrieved (retrieval miss).
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: 70.45 (Federal Register allocation notice, stay of the time limit, allocation order). Wrong section 740.10 was supplied and misapplied.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Give the picker each candidate's best-matching body sentence (by question n-gram overlap), not just its heading. Then run a post-pick check: if another candidate's body phrase overlap with the question ('levels proposed', 'all uses', 'petition') is substantially higher than the picked section's, include it alongside the pick or replace it. Also add a light procedural-intent cue: questions about a 'petition' should favor Parts 70/71 procedure sections over Part 740 labeling. All of this uses only question-to-candidate text signals, so it applies to any question that names no section. First check from the run logs whether 70.45 was a candidate. If it was not, the fix belongs in retrieval (body-text recall for sections with uninformative headings).

diagnoses.mechanism: The question names no substance ('a listed color additive' used at a higher level to hide degradation discoloration). The picker nevertheless chose 73.2329 (Guanine), a substance monograph, with 70.3(s) (area of the eye) as companion. Neither relates to the question. The key, 71.22 (a listing does not authorize use that may promote deception or conceal damage or inferiority), is absent. The question words 'hide' and 'degrades' are paraphrases of 'conceal' and 'damage/inferiority', so lexical recall for 71.22 is weak. The model then invented that the colorant was guanine and reasoned from GMP amounts. The validator correctly withheld the draft (unsupported_claim, provision_citation_mismatch). The packet does not show whether 71.22 was among the candidates.

diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: The correct draft (not requested to register under 710.9(a)) was withheld. The fallback omitted the 710.9 introduction and never stated the conclusion.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Count section headings shown in the evidence as supplied text for the support and invented_condition checks, and lemmatize there (exempt, exemption, exemptions). (2) Take nouns such as 'exemption' out of the condition-marker lexicon; keep real connectives (if, unless, provided, only when). (3) In a sentence that also has substantial overlap with a cited source, count words copied from the question's facts as supported, so application sentences are not scored as fabrications. (4) Fallback composer: always include a list parent's introductory text when quoting its items. Measure on the frozen set's FAIL drafts first, because the Phase 0 audit found the invented-condition path was a false-PASS route. These changes must not let unsupported regulatory content through.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker chose the right section and the full text of 720.1 was in the prompt (SOURCE 1: 'is requested to file Form FDA 2512 ... No filing fee is required'). The model turned the voluntary 'is requested to file' into a duty ('is required to file', 'is responsible for filing') and suggested the distributor is the party that has to file, although the source says any of manufacturer, packer or distributor. It also dropped the last sentence of the source, 'No filing fee is required'. The ANSWER FORMAT line ('say whether it is permitted or not, required or not') gives only a yes/no choice about obligation, with no option for 'requested' or 'should'. The validator raised only a low-overlap warning on the 700.3(b) sentence. No check compares how strong the obligation is in the answer against the source, so the escalated claim was delivered unchanged. The companion 700.3(b), forced in as an 'exhaustive' item, used up a whole sentence on an irrelevant definition.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong: 'requested' became 'required/responsible', and the distributor was implied to be the filer. Missing: either the manufacturer, packer or distributor may file; no filing fee is required.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add a check on obligation strength to the validator's operator layer. For each answer sentence that cites a source, compare the strength of the obligation stated about the same actor and action: 'is requested to', 'should', 'may' or 'voluntary' in the source, against 'must', 'shall', 'required', 'responsible for' or 'obligated' in the answer. Flag an escalation as an error, which sends the draft to repair with an instruction to keep the source's wording. Optionally add 'or only requested/recommended' to the ANSWER FORMAT choice. The check fires only when the cited source has no mandatory wording for that actor, so answers based on mandatory 'shall'/'must' sources are unaffected. It applies to all of Part 720 and to other voluntary programs (the 720.4-Q2 and 720.6-Q1 drafts also say 'must' where the source says 'should').

diagnoses.mechanism: The question names no section, so it went to the picker, which chose 720.9 ('Misbranding by reference to filing or to statement number'). That heading shares the words 'filing' and 'statement' with the question, but the section is about not implying FDA approval. The question asks about timing ('by when should it be filed'), and the section that answers it is 720.2 ('Times for filing'). 720.2 never reached the prompt (key in prompt = False). The picker's reply named a second section ('21 CFR 720.9, 21 CFR 7…', cut off in the packet), but only the first pick was kept. With only 720.9 and the 700.3(b) definition in front of it, the model correctly declined. The packet does not show the candidate list, so I cannot rule out that 720.2 was never a candidate (RETRIEVAL_MISSING).
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: 720.2 was missing: file within 60 days after commercial distribution begins (the 180-day window applied only to products already on the market). 720.9 was supplied instead.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Give the picker each candidate's heading plus the paragraph that best matches the query, and spell out what kind of answer the question needs ('by when' or 'how soon' calls for a time period or deadline) so that headings like 'Times for filing' outrank ones that merely share words. (2) Add a fallback that runs only on a decline: if the draft says the supplied provisions do not answer the question, re-run with the picker's next-ranked section and deliver that draft only if it passes the validator. Both changes leave questions that already get a correct pick or an answer untouched, because they apply only to the picker's ranking input and to drafts that decline.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker chose 720.6 ('Amendments to statement'), whose opening sentence ('should be submitted by filing an amended Form FDA 2512') shares words with 'a company filing Form FDA 2512 should do'. The text that actually answers the question is in 720.4(b), 'The person filing Form FDA 2512 should: (1)…(4)', which is deep inside 720.4. That section's heading and opening ((a), what the form asks for) do not look like the question, and 'Beyond completing the form' points exactly past (a) to (b). Only 720.6 was in the prompt. The model answered from it with confidence and gave no notice that amendment timing is not what was asked.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: All of 720.4(b) was missing: give the (a) information, have the form signed by an authorized person, provide ingredient or treatment information to poison control centers, and provide ingredient information or samples to a treating physician. 720.6 amendment and discontinuance timing was given instead.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Build each picker candidate's preview from its best-matching paragraph(s), scored against the question at paragraph level, rather than from the section heading and opening text. Here 720.4(b) matches 'filing Form FDA 2512 should' almost word for word. Also let the paragraph-level match break ties between sections in the same Part. This reuses existing paragraph rows and changes only what the picker sees. Picks that are already right because of the heading are unaffected, because a matching heading still appears. Measure on the 352-row set and the 100-question holdout for picks that get lost.

diagnoses.mechanism: The full text of 720.6 was in the prompt: 'Other changes do not justify immediate amendment, but should be shown by filing an amended Form FDA 2512 within a year after such changes.' The model read only the first half of that sentence and concluded that the office move 'does not trigger any amendment obligation'; it dropped the 'but … within a year' clause. The validator flagged that sentence (unsupported_claim error, 20%), and repair removed it from the second paragraph. But the repair rewrote the same false claim into the first paragraph ('does not affect the timing or necessity of the amendment … No other action is required for the office move'), and nothing re-checked it. The short sentence 'No other action is required for the office move.' was never flagged, probably because of a minimum length or the support check skipping uncited sentences in the lead paragraph.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong: 'No other action is required for the office move.' Missing: other changes, such as the address, should be shown on an amended Form 2512 within a year.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Extend qualifier_dropped so it also covers contrasting 'X do not …, but should Y' clauses. When a cited source attaches a second obligation after 'but', 'however' or 'except that', an answer that denies any obligation for that class ('no action required', 'does not trigger') is flagged as a contradiction error. (2) After repair, re-validate every sentence of the repaired text against the error that started the repair, including short and uncited sentences. Repair must not paraphrase the claim it was told to remove. Both changes fire only on denials of an obligation that contradict a clause in the source, so correct answers are untouched.

diagnoses.mechanism: All of 740.10(a)-(c) was supplied (SOURCE 7 is (c): 'Paragraph (b) … does not constitute an exemption to the adulteration provisions …'). The model stated the three (b) conditions correctly but never mentioned (c). The prompt's answer plan led it to skip (c): the 'its sub-requirements' line lists only sources [2],[4],[5],[6], and 'conditions to keep' has only 'unless' [1], so the limiting clause in (c) was never marked as something the answer must cover. Repair rewrote the first paragraph after the validator errors and also left out (c). The focused-answer completeness check did not flag the missing paragraph.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: 740.10(c), meaning (b) is not an exemption from the Act's adulteration provisions or any other requirement.
diagnoses.fix_detail: In the answer-plan extractor, recognize saving and limiting clauses ('does not constitute an exemption', 'nothing in this paragraph', 'does not relieve', 'is not an exemption from') in any EXACT paragraph of the requested section. Emit them under 'limits to keep' and make the focused-answer completeness check (_focus_gap) require them when the answer relies on the paragraph they limit (here (b)). The change is narrow and pattern-based: it adds a required item only when such a clause is present, so other sections' plans stay byte-identical.

diagnoses.mechanism: The model's draft was correct: the full caution appeared in both paragraphs, along with the duty to give adequate directions for safe use and the optional (c) wording. The validator found nothing, yet the delivered text differs from the draft. In the second paragraph the caution was cut to 'Caution—Use only as directed. Keep out of reach of children [3].' The three removed sentences ('Excessive use…', 'Discontinue use…', 'Consult your physician…') are exactly the ones that already appeared word for word inside the quotation in the first paragraph. The two kept sentences differ in form (the 'Caution—' prefix and the [3] marker). This points to a deterministic sentence-level duplicate-removal step in output post-processing (enforcing 'Say each point once') that split a verbatim regulatory statement into sentences and deleted the repeats, producing a shortened caution that contradicts the full one.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Wrong: the second paragraph presents the required caution as only 'Use only as directed. Keep out of reach of children.'
diagnoses.fix_detail: Make duplicate removal treat quoted or mandated statement text as one unit: never delete a sentence that sits inside a quotation or a block quoted from an EXACT source (detect by quotes, or by a match of four or more words against the source); remove only whole duplicated claims or whole duplicated quotations. After post-processing, check that every quoted span which matched source text before the step still matches it without gaps; if not, roll back to the pre-step text. This affects every required-warning section (740.11-740.19, colour-additive label statements) and cannot hurt answers whose quotes are left intact.

diagnoses.mechanism: The prompt holds 740.18(a), the warning text, (b) (including 2,4-diaminoanisole sulfate) and 740.2(a)/(b), but nothing about the eCFR note that 740.18 was stayed until further notice effective Sept. 18, 1980 (47 FR 7829). The words 'stay', 'stayed' and 'effective' appear nowhere in the evidence. Either ingestion dropped the section's editorial or effective-date note, or packing does not attach it. The question asks outright 'is it in effect?'. Without the note, the model did not say that the evidence leaves the status open, which the prompt rule 'say which part they leave open' asks for. It declared 'the product in question is subject to the warning requirement', which is the wrong answer to the status question.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: the stay until further notice, effective Sept. 18, 1980 (47 FR 7829). Wrong: the answer asserts the warning requirement applies now.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Ingest eCFR section-level notes (effective-date notes, stays, suspensions, 'EDITORIAL NOTE') as status metadata for the section. Have the evidence packer put a short 'Status:' line at the head of every EXACT source for a section that carries one; it costs few characters and is outside the paragraph budget. Add a validator check: when the question asks whether a provision is in effect or still applies and no status line is present, an answer asserting current applicability is flagged and repaired to say the status is not shown. Sections without notes are unchanged.

diagnoses.mechanism: The full text of 740.2(a) and (b) was supplied, and the draft's first paragraph had every key element: prominent and conspicuous, bold type on a contrasting background, at least 1/16 inch, unless (b) applies. The model then rambled through three more paragraphs. It contradicted itself ('The regulation does not specify that warnings must be in a particular size'), went too far ('use of italic text is not authorized'), added a decline, and was cut off mid-sentence. The validator withheld the draft, but its three errors fell mostly on content that is substantively fine. Two condition_not_in_cited_source errors were raised because the exemption sentences cite [2], and (b) does not use the word 'exemption', although (a) says 'exemption pursuant to paragraph (b)'. One unsupported_claim error hit the 'These provisions impose none of…' sentence, which the ANSWER FORMAT itself tells the model to write. The false size sentence drew only a low-overlap warning. Withholding was the right outcome for this draft, but the error flags missed the bad sentences and hit the good ones, so a sentence-level repair would remove the correct core instead.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Delivered nothing: the 740.2(a) requirements were never shown. The draft wrongly claimed there is no size requirement and that italic is prohibited, and ended truncated.
diagnoses.fix_detail: (1) Resolve cross-references within a section in condition_not_in_cited_source: if the cited paragraph is the target of a condition in a sibling paragraph ('exemption pursuant to paragraph (b)'), citing it for that condition is valid. (2) Classify statements that a provision imposes nothing ('these provisions impose none', 'no provision requires X') as absence claims. Verify them by checking that no supplied source carries an obligation about X, instead of by word overlap. This also fixes the false flag in UC-COS-024. (3) Add a contradiction check between answer sentences and source numbers or limits ('does not specify … size' against 'in no case … less than 1/16 inch'). With the errors placed on the right sentences, sentence-level repair can keep the correct first paragraph and drop the contradictory and truncated tail. Never salvage a truncated loop prefix as such. Measure on the 352-row set for wrong answers newly delivered before switching it on.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker chose the right section, but 700.27 is larger than the budget ('7 paragraphs left out'). The packet holds (c), (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(4) and (c)(6), but (c)(3) (records kept at the establishment or a reasonably accessible location), (c)(5) (available to FDA for inspection and copying) and (d) (non-compliance makes the product adulterated under 601(c)) are absent. Meanwhile the budget went to definition paragraphs that do not bear on a records question: (a)(3) MS beef, (a)(4) nonambulatory cattle, (a)(5) SRM, (b)(2) small intestine. (a)(6) on its own carries about 900 characters of incorporation-by-reference boilerplate (AOCS address, FDA library address, NARA phone number and URL). The question's focus terms ('records', 'keep') match the heading of the (c) subtree exactly, but packing did not keep that subtree together. The model also merged (a)(6) into the records duty and turned its 'or' test into 'and' (the delivered text reads 'no more than 0.15 percent … and that it is not derived').
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: record location ((c)(3)), FDA inspection and copying ((c)(5)), adulteration for non-compliance ((d)/601(c)). Wrong: the tallow test is stated with 'and' instead of 'or'.
diagnoses.fix_detail: When a requested section exceeds the budget, rank its paragraphs as subtrees. A headed paragraph whose heading matches the question's focus terms ('(c) Records.') is packed together with all its children first, then the operative requirement and consequence paragraphs ((b), (d)), then definitions. Strip incorporation-by-reference availability boilerplate (where to get copies: addresses, phone numbers, URLs) from EXACT text before measuring it against the budget. Sections that fit whole are byte-identical. For the conjunction error, extend the existing contradiction operators to flag an answer that uses 'and' where the cited source uses 'or' between alternative requirements. The earlier grouped-subparagraph packing was rejected (0 gained, 3 lost), so A/B this on the 352-row set and the 100-question holdout.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker returned '21 CFR 740.18, FD&C Act §'. It listed a CFR section first and then started naming a statute section, but the reply stops at '§', which looks like a short output-token cap. The parser kept only the first ID (740.18). 740.18 looked plausible because the question says 'coal-tar hair dye' and 'label', but it is the cancer-warning rule for 2,4-diaminoanisole, not the 601(a) hair-dye proviso. The prompt holds only 740.18(a)/(b) and 740.2(a)/(b); it has no 'preliminary test', 'eyelashes' or 'blindness' text. The question was also rewritten to end '(21 CFR 740.18, 740.2)', which tied the model to the wrong section. The draft answered faithfully from 740.18, so it was wrong for the question. The validator withheld it for provision_citation_mismatch, and that finding looks false. The flagged sentence names § 740.2, but its cited source 740.18(a) itself says 'in accordance with the requirements of § 740.2'. Also, line 67 ends in '."' and the next line starts with a digit ('21 CFR ...'), so two sentences probably merged into one.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: FD&C Act 601(a) proviso is missing: the conspicuous caution statement (skin irritation; preliminary test; not for eyelashes or eyebrows, may cause blindness) and adequate directions for the preliminary test. 740.18 was answered in its place.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Make the picker output one candidate index from an enumerated list (constrained choice), not free-text IDs, so the reply cannot be cut off or list several sections. Alternatively, raise its token cap, parse every ID it names, and when it names both a CFR section and a statute section, promote both as r1/r2 (the prompt here had spare budget). Separately, provision_citation_mismatch should accept a section name that appears as a cross-reference inside the cited source's text, and the sentence splitter should treat '."' followed by a digit-led citation as a sentence boundary. Both changes apply to every question and only restore candidates the picker already chose; check them against the frozen 352-row set for lost correct picks.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker reply '21 CFR 700.27, FD&C Act §' is cut off the same way as Q1, and only the CFR ID was kept. 700.27 (prohibited cattle materials) looked plausible only because its paragraph (d) is headed 'Adulteration' and points to 'section 601(c) of the act'. The prompt has no 601(b), (c) or (d) text; it has no 'filthy', 'insanitary' or 'container is composed' text. The question was rewritten to end '(21 CFR 700.27)'. The draft correctly said 700.27 does not cover rodent filth or the resin. The validator withheld it because those scope-limiting sentences scored 0-20% content-word overlap. Even if delivered, the answer would have FAILed, because it never supplies the 601(b)-(d) grounds. The evidence budget was also spent on 700.27 definitions (7 paragraphs left out).
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: FD&C Act 601(b) filthy/putrid/decomposed, 601(c) insanitary conditions, 601(d) poisonous or deleterious container are all missing; the evidence was the unrelated 700.27.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Same mechanism as COS-FDCA601-Q1: a constrained single-index picker output, or parse all IDs and promote both the CFR and the statute section. As a backstop, add a companion rule: when a promoted CFR paragraph cross-references an FD&C Act section that exists in the statute corpus ('section 601(c) of the act'), add that statute subsection as a companion if budget allows. Cross-reference-driven companions are general and bounded by the existing budget.

diagnoses.mechanism: The pick was right and 608(a), (b) and (c) are in the prompt. SOURCE 3 is labelled only '608(c)' but contains (1) and (2) inline. The model had to invent paragraph labels and called the last sentence of (c)(2), on cumulative exposure, '608(c)(3)', a paragraph that does not exist. The validator accepted it, apparently because (c)(3) reads as a child of the cited 608(c). The model's (c)(1) paraphrase also dropped 'sufficient to support a reasonable certainty that a cosmetic product is safe', although that text is in SOURCE 3 (prompt line 297). The 601(g) consequence (adulterated without substantiation) is not in the prompt at all. 601(g) refers to 608, but 608 does not refer back, so the forward cross-reference companions did not add it. Separately, the validator's invented_condition error on 'except coal-tar hair dye' was a false positive: 608(b) says subsection (a) 'shall not apply' to coal-tar hair dye.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: The answer cites a nonexistent 608(c)(3), drops the 'reasonable certainty that the product is safe' standard of (c)(1), and omits that the product is adulterated under 601(g) without substantiation.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Split statute subsections that contain enumerated paragraphs into paragraph-level sources (608(c)(1), 608(c)(2)), as eCFR text already is, so the model copies citations instead of making them up. Add a validator check that every paragraph designator named in the answer exists in the supplied source text, which would flag (c)(3). Optionally, add reverse cross-reference companions: statute subsections that cite the requested section, such as 601(g) citing 608. Paragraph splitting changes only citation granularity; the 601(g) companion needs a budget check.

diagnoses.mechanism: The pick was right and the full 610(a) text is in the prompt, and the answer covers every 610(a) element. One delivered sentence says the requirement 'does not extend to records related to a facility that solely performs labeling, relabeling, packaging, repackaging, holding, or distributing' and cites [1] (610(a)). That content comes from SOURCE 3 (604(3)(B)(viii), the facility definition), and the model reframed a definition exclusion as a records exclusion. The validator did not catch it: it judges support against any supplied source rather than the cited one, and citation re-pointing did not fire. The skeptic scorer also claimed the data-exclusion list belongs to 610(b), but in the prompt that sentence ('This subsection shall not be construed to extend to recipes...') is inside 610(a). That scorer reason is wrong, although the plain scorer's PP reason is valid on its own.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: The 604(3)(B)(viii) facility carve-out is cited to 610(a) and misframed as a records exclusion. Nothing in the key is missing.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add a cited-source attribution test. When a sentence's distinctive content words (here labeling, relabeling, repackaging, holding, distributing) occur only in a non-cited supplied source, and overlap with the cited source is much lower, either re-point the citation to that source using the existing two-source re-pointing guard, or flag the sentence for repair. This is general and only rewrites citation numbers. Do not 'correct' the exclusion list to 610(b): the skeptic is wrong on that point.

diagnoses.mechanism: The pick was right (named_statute) and 610(a) is in the prompt in full. The raw draft fell into a repetitive loop and stopped mid-sentence at the token limit ('These provisions do not impose'). The delivered answer is a rewritten, condensed version. It keeps the 'yes' and the conditions, but drops the one draft sentence that said what the duty is (draft line 455: a designated officer, on credentials and written notice, may access all records relating to the product). That sentence was not among the validator findings, so the condense or correction step removed unflagged key content. The answer also never uses 604(3)(C) (filling is not 'packaging'), which bears directly on a contract filler, though the key does not require it.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: The answer never states the duty itself: letting a designated officer access and copy records relating to the product and similarly affected products, as needed for the adulteration and threat determination.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Make the repair/condense pass coverage-preserving. A draft sentence that no finding flagged, and that is the only sentence covering a given source clause (by content-word overlap with the operative 'shall ... permit ... access to and copy' clause), must be kept verbatim. Only flagged or duplicate sentences may be dropped or rewritten. To cut the looping that triggers condensing, add a repetition stop at generation (stop when the same sentence frame repeats N times) instead of truncating. Both changes only restrict what the repair step may delete, so they cannot remove supported content elsewhere.

diagnoses.mechanism: The pick was right and 611(a)-(h) are all in the prompt, including 611(a)'s 'opportunity to voluntarily cease distribution and recall' and the 'If the responsible person refuses to or does not voluntarily...' condition, and 611(c)(3) 'amend the order to require a recall'. The model said 611(a) lets the Secretary order 'cessation of distribution or recall ... even if the responsible person refuses to act voluntarily'. That puts recall into 611(a), which authorises only an order to cease distribution, and blurs the voluntary-first precondition. The draft's first paragraph had the correct conditional ('if they refuse or do not voluntarily comply within the time and manner prescribed'), but the delivered version rewrote that unflagged sentence into the 'even if' wording. The model also skipped 611(c) (recall by amended order after the hearing), even though the answer format asks it to go paragraph by paragraph.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: The answer omits that FDA must first offer voluntary cessation and recall, says recall is ordered under 611(a) when it comes by amended order under 611(c)(3) after the 611(b) hearing, and never mentions 611(c).
diagnoses.fix_detail: Add two general checks. (1) Condition inversion: when the cited source makes a power conditional ('If ... refuses ... the Secretary may'), flag answer sentences that say 'even if', 'regardless' or 'without', or that state the power unconditionally, using the existing condition and qualifier machinery. (2) Paragraph coverage: when a supplied requested-provision paragraph contains a focus verb or noun from the question (here 'recall' in 611(c)) and no answer sentence cites it, trigger repair to add one sentence for it. Also apply the splice-only repair rule so unflagged correct sentences are never rewritten. These checks fire only on missing or contradicted conditions, so faithful answers are unaffected.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker returned 'FD&C Act § 613' (exemption for products and facilities also subject to drug/device rules) instead of 612 (small businesses). The question's 'small-business test' and 'sales' match 612's subject, and 613 probably looked plausible as another 'exemption' section. The packet does not show the candidate list, so whether 612 was offered is unverified. With 613(a)/(b) and 604(3) as evidence, a deterministic value gate read 'Which figure counts' as a request for an amount, found none, and returned value_not_established without calling the model. Even with 612 in the evidence, that gate would probably have answered '$1,000,000' instead of choosing between the user's own figures.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: 612(a) is missing: average gross annual U.S. cosmetic-product sales over the previous 3 years, under $1,000,000 adjusted for inflation, so the $800,000 figure counts; the 612(b) product condition is also missing.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Give the picker each statute candidate's heading and its first subsection sentence. Add a post-pick guard: if the chosen candidate shares no heading terms with the question while another candidate's heading strongly matches question terms ('small business(es)'), take the matching one or ask the picker again. Narrow the value-question gate so that questions comparing figures the user supplied ('which figure counts', 'does X or Y apply') go to the model instead of the amount-lookup path. Both are general routing rules; measure on the 352-row set for lost picks.

diagnoses.mechanism: The picker reply '21 CFR 80.39, FD&C Act § 6' is cut off just before the statute section number, almost certainly 610, which exists in the statute corpus and was used for the 610 questions. The parser took the first ID, 80.39 (color-additive batch distribution records). It looked plausible because it shares 'records', 'upon the request of any officer or employee of the FDA' and 'reasonable hours'. The question was rewritten to end '(21 CFR 80.39)'. The prompt has no 610 text and no personnel-data exclusion. The model faithfully said 80.39 does not reach training files. The validator withheld it for 0-20% overlap on those scope statements. Even if delivered, the answer would have failed.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: The answer misses the FD&C Act 610(a) records-access conditions (reasonable belief of adulteration with a serious-threat risk, credentials and written notice), and the personnel-data exclusion with its exception for qualifications of technical and professional personnel. It also misses 704 inspection.
diagnoses.fix_detail: Same picker-output fix as COS-FDCA601-Q1/Q2: a constrained single-index choice, or full parsing with both the CFR and statute IDs promoted. This is the third packet case where a truncated reply discarded the statute section the picker was naming, so the fix targets a recurring mechanism, not this question. Also stop appending the picked section to the question text, since that pushes the model toward a possibly wrong pick; keep it only under REQUESTED PROVISIONS.

diagnoses.mechanism: No section was promoted (picked=none, method=None), so the picker never ran on any statute candidate. The prompt holds only off-domain discovery: a device ultrasound guidance, a PET drug media-fill guidance and 21 CFR 349.78 (OTC eyewash labeling). There is no 606, 601(a) or 601(c) text. The question's words ('mixers, homogenizers, filling machines', 'certified') do not overlap the statute text, so lexical retrieval surfaced unrelated sterilization and filling material. The model said 'No' with no citation and then said the sources were insufficient. The validator removed the explanatory sentences, leaving a self-contradictory answer. Part of the key (606 GMP rule not yet issued; FDA does not certify equipment) is a status or absence fact that no statute text states, so even perfect retrieval would have reached partial credit at best.
diagnoses.missing_or_wrong: Missing: no codified equipment-certification requirement; the 606 GMP mandate (rule not issued); 601(c) insanitary conditions and 601(a) deleterious substances as the duties that do apply. The answer has no citation and contradicts itself.
diagnoses.fix_detail: For general questions about a cosmetic product (lotions, shampoo), add statute candidates through a heading-level index of the FD&C Act cosmetics chapter (606 'Good manufacturing practice' for manufacturing, equipment or facility vocabulary; 601 'Adulterated cosmetics'). Down-rank discovery from other product domains (device and drug guidance, OTC drug parts such as Part 349) when the question's product is a cosmetic. This applies across all general cosmetics questions; check that it does not push guidance the scorers judged relevant out of the budget on the 352-row set.

diagnoses.mechanism: No section was promoted (picked=none, method=None), so the picker never ran because there was no section-level candidate. The prompt holds three DISCOVERY sources: a drug quality-agreement guidance, a CVM animal-drug batch guidance, and 21 CFR 341.80(d)(2)(iv)(A)(2), which concerns nasal decongestant labeling and was matched only on 'calibrated dropper'. Lexical retrieval matched 'calibrat', 'batch' and 'contract' to drug documents. FD&C Act 606 is nowhere in the prompt, and nothing says Parts 700-740 hold no calibration provision. Given this evidence the model correctly declined. The delivered answer is just the decline sentence, because the scoped-absence sentence after it was flagged and dropped. synthesis:
# Holdout 100Q failure analysis (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, 37 PASS)

## Summary

- **63 questions did not pass: 8 partially pass, 26 partially fail and 29 fail.** For 27 of them the prompt never had the right evidence: the picker chose wrongly 18 times, packing or companions left gaps 5 times, and retrieval missed 4 times. The other 36 failed after the evidence stage: the model misread or left things out (20), the validator or repair step blocked or damaged the answer (11), citations were wrong (3), or the composer erred (2). In 34 of those 36 the text that answers the question was in the prompt.
- **When the key section is in the prompt, the 4B model passes about 46% of the time (37 of 80). When it is missing, it never passes (0 of 20).** I use this as the prior for any fix that only gets evidence into the prompt.
- **The cheapest and safest gains come from changes that can be measured offline on recorded drafts, with no regeneration.** These are validator false positives, the composer and post-processing, a correction pass limited to flagged sentences, and checks that drop a wrong sentence. Together they are worth about 8 PASS on paper.
- **If every fix shipped and every diagnosis were right, the gain would be +16.7.** I would plan for **+8 on this set (about 45/100) and +5 to +7 on a fresh, similar set.** The reasons for the discount are in section 2.
- **Withholding helped users overall.** Of the 19 withheld drafts, 10 were misleading and 3 would have passed. But 5 of those 10 were blocked by findings that are themselves false, or that the proposed validator fixes would relax. That is why the regression gates name those rows one by one.

Method note: the stage and fix counts come from single-pass per-question diagnoses (33 high, 29 medium and 1 low confidence). They agree with the measured 18 wrong picks.

---

## 1. Count tables

### Primary root-cause stage

|---|---|---|
| PICK_WRONG_SECTION | 18 | 0 / 3 / 15 |
| MODEL_MISREAD | 14 | 14 / 0 / 0 |
| VALIDATOR_BLOCKED_GOOD_DRAFT | 9 | 8 / 1 / 0 |
| MODEL_INCOMPLETE | 6 | 6 / 0 / 0 |
| EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE | 5 | 0 / 5 / 0 |
| RETRIEVAL_MISSING | 4 | 0 / 1 / 3 |
| CITATION_ERROR | 3 | 2 / 1 / 0 |
| VALIDATOR_BLOCKED_BAD_DRAFT | 2 | 2 / 0 / 0 |
| COMPOSER_ERROR | 2 | 2 / 0 / 0 |
| **Total** | **63** | **34 / 11 / 18** |

The measured "key section in prompt" split is 42 / 1 / 20. It is higher than the diagnosis count of 34 because 8 rows had the section in the prompt but not the paragraph that answers the question. For example, 70.3-Q2 had only paragraph (l), and 701.3-Q3 lacked the (g) siblings.

### Fix class (from the diagnoses)

### Category by primary stage (where the failures sit)

| Category (PASS) | Non-PASS | Pick | Misread | Incomplete | Validator good/bad | Evidence | Retrieval | Citation | Composer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Colour listings (23/35) | 12 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 4 / 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

*The four named categories add up to 97, so I placed the remaining three rows here by inference.

What the table says:
- **Colour listings:** a third of the failures are validator false positives. These are cheap to fix.
- **Statute:** most failures are picking or candidate problems.
- **Labeling:** the largest group is model reading with complete evidence. Pipeline work will buy little PASS there.

---

## 2. Fixes ranked by expected PASS gain

**How I estimated.** Each of the 63 rows is assigned to exactly one fix: 59 rows to fixes, and 4 rows to section 3 with no gain counted. The probability next to each row is my estimate that it becomes PASS given that fix. "Also needs" notes a dependency, but the row is still counted once.

For fixes that only get evidence into the prompt, I capped the probability near the 0.46 prior. Statute and labeling rows get less than that, colour listings slightly more.

**Regression gates.** Every fix below names the gates it must pass before shipping.
- **G1 Validator replay (offline, exact).** Re-run the recorded drafts from the 100Q holdout, the 300-row validator set, dev34 and dev_label. To pass:
  - The 37 holdout PASS rows deliver byte-identical text.
  - These rows stay withheld: 74.2101, 70.19, 70.3-Q2, 70.45, 71.22, 740.2, FDCA601-Q1, FDCA601-Q2, UC-002, UC-014, plus SD-007.
  - Every row whose delivered text changes is blind double-scored, and none becomes misleading.
  - Unit tests: 792 pass, with the same 6 known failures.
- **G2 Check calibration.** Any new error-level check fires 0 times on sentences of PASS answers in the holdout and dev sets. Warnings are allowed but must be listed. This is the same standard as the validator audit, where 31 of 33 fires were on FAIL and none on PASS.
- **G3 Evidence replay.** On the 352-question retrieval baseline, the byte-level compare differs only on a trigger list declared in advance. On the 277-question cosmetics replay, no keyed section is lost.
- **G4 Picker replay.** Run the picker on the 100Q and 352 sets. None of the 38 currently right picks may change, and every changed pick is listed and checked by hand.
- **G5 Regeneration A/B.** Regenerate only the rows whose prompt changed (in the 100Q, dev34 and dev_label sets) on Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, both arms with the same configuration, blind double-scored. Accept only if PASS gained is at least twice PASS lost, no PASS row becomes misleading, and no must-refuse row is delivered.

### Ranking

| # | Fix | Rows | Expected PASS | How measured | Regression risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A. Validator precision on correct drafts | 10 | **4.65** | offline (G1) | medium, with named traps |
| 2 | B. Picker hardening (name guard, untruncated reply) | 9 | **2.10** | regenerate | medium |
| 3 | G. Composer and post-processing | 4 | **1.70** | 1.15 offline, 0.55 regenerate | low |
| 4 | H. Content-aware picker | 8 | **1.55** | regenerate | **high** |
| 5 | E. Checks that drop a wrong sentence | 6 | **1.40** | offline | medium |
| 6 | F2. Packing that keeps paragraph structure | 6 | **1.40** | regenerate | medium-high |
| 7 | C. Pointer and delegation companions | 3 | **1.05** | regenerate | medium |
| 8 | F1. Evidence-text bugs | 3 | **0.90** | regenerate | low-medium |
| 9 | D. Correction pass limited to flagged sentences | 4 | **0.85** | offline | medium |
| 10 | J. Answer-plan prompt fixes | 3 | **0.80** | regenerate | medium |
| 11 | I. Statute topic-alias candidates | 3 | **0.25** | regenerate | low; not worth it now |
| | **Sum** | **59** | **16.65** | offline 8.05 / regenerate 8.60 | |

**Why I plan for about +8 rather than +16.7.**
- **Diagnoses may be wrong.** 30 of the 63 are medium or low confidence, and 9 picker diagnoses could not see the candidate list.
- **Regenerated changes have netted about zero here before.** The binding_first, heading_relevance and trigram threshold changes, context packing and the general-format switch all came out at +4 or less once losses were counted.
- **The rules were designed on these exact rows.** I apply about 65% to the offline fixes (about +5.2) and about 35% net to the regenerated ones (about +3.0).
- **The holdout is now a dev set.** Once these fixes are designed against these 63 rows, an honest gain estimate needs a fresh, unseen set.

### Fix details

**1. A. Validator precision on correct drafts (expected 4.65, offline)**
- **Rows:** 82.1328 (.8), 73.2120 (.65), 71.30 (.6), 82.1602 (.45), 82.1330 (.4), 700.27-Q3 (.4), 70.10 (.4), 700.3-Q2 (.35), FDCA610-Q1 (.3), 710.9 (.3, only after B ships).
- **Rules:**
  - **A1. Citation numbers in the figure check.** Reduce '§ 74.1328 (a)(1)', '§74.1328(a)(1)' and '74.1328' to the same citation before comparing. Numbers in Citation and Heading labels count as supplied text.
  - **A2. Scoped absence statements.** Check "this/these provision(s) impose/set/specify no X" by confirming the cited source has no limiting term for X, instead of using word overlap. Unscoped denials ("there is no X", "no regulation anywhere") stay errors; unscoped denials caused the earlier false-denial regression.
  - **A3. Drop filler sentences.** Remove whole sentences that carry no citation, fail support, are not the first sentence, or repeat a supported sentence. Then re-validate and re-check completeness. Never remove a clause inside a sentence, because that is the invented_conditions_removed false-PASS route.
  - **A4. Re-point citations.** Fix the bracket number when the sentence explicitly names a provision held by exactly one other supplied source (71.30), when a source number was mistaken for a paragraph label (700.27-Q3), or when the sentence's distinctive words come from another source (FDCA610-Q1).
  - **A5.** Count headings as supplied text, match word forms (exempt, exemption), and take 'exemption' out of the list of condition words (710.9).
  - **A6.** Derive "every item must be covered" obligations only from listing wording in the user's question, never from citations that section promotion inserted (700.3-Q2).
- **Traps:** each item below is a protection that a naive version of A would remove. Each must be designed out and checked in G1.

## 4. Did withholding protect users?

**Yes, on balance.** Here is how the 19 withheld drafts score if they had been shown:

| If shown | n | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| Would pass (citations right, substance 2, completeness 2, not misleading) | 3 | 73.2120, 82.1328, 71.30 |
| Near pass, only a citation defect | 1 | 700.27-Q3 |
| Right direction but incomplete or on the wrong basis; not misleading | 5 | 70.10, 701.13-Q2, UC-008, UC-010, 82.3 |
| **Misleading** (5 of them also fabricate) | **10** | 74.2101†, 70.45†, 740.2†, FDCA601-Q1†, UC-002†, 70.19, 70.3-Q2, 71.22, FDCA601-Q2, UC-014 |

† also fabricates.

- **Withholding blocked 10 misleading answers at a cost of 3–4 passes.** 53% of the withheld drafts were misleading, against 65% (20 of 31) on the dev questions earlier today. The conclusion is the same: do not loosen thresholds across the board.
- **The validator mainly backstops the picker.** 8 of the 10 misleading drafts come from a wrong pick. The validator withheld 9 of the 18 wrong-pick drafts, and 8 of those were misleading. B therefore reduces how much users depend on withholding.
- **Half of the protection is accidental.**
  - 70.19 was blocked by a false '75' figure.
  - FDCA601-Q1 was blocked by a citation mismatch that is itself probably false.
  - FDCA601-Q2 and UC-002 were blocked by low overlap on scope negatives, the very mechanism A2 relaxes.
  - UC-014 was blocked by a shaky 'exempt' invented-condition finding that A5 removes.
  - In 740.2 the errors landed on the correct sentences.

  This is why G1 lists these rows by name and why A has a fixed order.
- **There is a hidden cost beyond the 19.** Four more correct drafts were replaced by the verbatim fallback (82.1330, 82.705, 700.3-Q2, 710.9). Six more were damaged by the correction pass: 82.1602, 701.11, FDCA611, FDCA610-Q2 and 720.6 were damaged, and UC-018 lost its scope caveat.
- **The protection covers only one kind of error.** About 20 of the 44 delivered non-PASS answers contain a substantive misstatement, judged by the diagnoses rather than blind-scored. Examples:
  - a condition turned into a premise (73.2087, 73.2329);
  - 'should', 'requested' or 'may' turned into 'must' or 'prohibited' (720.1, 701.1, 710.3, 82.51);
  - an exception moved to another paragraph (700.25-Q1);
  - a wrong date (700.25-Q3);
  - a shortened mandatory caution (740.17);
  - an invented condition (80.22, 82.5);
  - "no other action required" (720.6).

  These sentences share many words with the source, so the overlap-based validator passes them. E is aimed at about 9 of them, which is why I would ship it even though its PASS gain is small.
